integrated-rate-law.def: An equation linking a reactant concentration to time, such as ln[A]t − ln[A]0 = −kt for a first-order reaction.

rate-plot.def: The graph of concentration data that comes out as a straight line for a given order: [A] vs t (zero), ln[A] vs t (first) or 1/[A] vs t (second). Its slope gives k.

half-life.def: The time for a reactant concentration to fall to half its value. For a first-order reaction it is constant: t½ = 0.693/k.
